notes: Run time = stop-to-stop chainage ÷ stated average speed, including accel/braking: tram 10 m/s, sky rail 12 m/s. Starting values [S], tune by playtest.
Headway (tram 120 s, sky rail 90 s) and dwell (tram 15 s, sky rail 12 s) are my starting values; the GDD gives none. Motive/Keel to confirm.
Journey sec = in-vehicle run time plus dwell at intermediate stops only. It excludes waiting for a vehicle, interchange walking and any boarding cost, none of which the GDD sets.
Reverse journeys are assumed symmetric; reverse runs are listed for every line.
Interchange pairs: T1/records-T2/market, T1/circus-S1/circus, T2/parade-S1/harbour. 'via' names the stop on the arriving line.
T1 and T2 are through-running, with termini off-sheet. T1 chainage ends at the circus loop, and the loop is not timed. S1's Skyport balloon loop is not timed.
Only stops on the sheet are timetabled; vehicles beyond the sheet are not modelled.

openQuestions.question: Does boarding a tram or sky rail as fast travel cost anything (cash, Trail, Alert, cooldown), and is it limited by where the player can board?
openQuestions.why: Datum's hold includes boarding as fast travel but the GDD sets no price or rule, so none is written into the timetable.

openQuestions.question: Is boarding as fast travel a player power at all, and does the cell wait for the scheduled vehicle or ride an instant hop?
openQuestions.why: This is a design decision outside the timetable. Journey times assume the cell waits for a real vehicle and are in-vehicle only.

openQuestions.question: Do the timetable headway and dwell values need to match any mission window, e.g. the handover timings?
openQuestions.why: The starting headways and dwells are my own and are not drawn from the GDD.
